Short answer: Keep first. Connect second. Replace third. Build last. Each step costs more attention, so the bigger move needs better evidence.

What this means for your business

A tool can be imperfect and still be the correct tool. Change is justified when the present workflow creates enough cost, risk, or customer friction to beat the migration and care burden.

What to watch

  • A new tool proposed before the current job is mapped.
  • An integration that creates a second source of truth.
  • A replacement with no data exit or staff training plan.
  • Custom software built for a problem that happens twice a year.

Do this next

  1. Name the broken outcome, not the disliked tool.
  2. Measure one week of handoffs, delays, errors, and cost.
  3. Test the smallest move that fixes the outcome.
  4. Name ownership, maintenance, migration, and exit before buying.

When Little Fight fits

This is how we scope every systems job. The answer can be no project. That is still a useful answer.
